result.summary: Make ThreadOpenConnections wait while network activity is disabled instead of continuously executing its loop. This prevents the connection loop from popping and discarding configured seednodes and address-fetch entries while the node cannot open connections.
result.problem: When the network is inactive (via -networkactive=0 or setnetworkactive false), ThreadOpenConnections continues looping and pops seednodes into addr-fetch queues, which are then dropped by OpenNetworkConnection. Once network activity is re-enabled, all seednodes have been exhausted without ever being contacted, preventing addr-fetch attempts until the node is restarted.
evidence: Author description explains the mechanism: 'With < 2 outbound peers or an empty addrman, a seednode is popped from seed_nodes, queued as an addr-fetch, and then popped again from m_addr_fetches in ProcessAddrFetch(). It is then dropped because OpenNetworkConnection() returns early when the network is inactive. Once the network is re-enabled, no seednodes remain.'
Author notes precedent in merged PR #34213, where 'Anchors were lost in the same way before #34213.'
result.scope_notes: Small patch (+24/-19) adding a wait condition on network activity in ThreadOpenConnections and an accompanying test.
result.card: ThreadOpenConnections now pauses while network activity is disabled rather than running continuously. Previously, disabling the network caused the connection loop to pop and discard seednodes and addr-fetch queues when OpenNetworkConnection rejected them, leaving the node without seednodes after the network was re-enabled until restarted. The PR mirrors the fix from PR #34213 which addressed an identical issue with anchor connections.

risk.why: Flaws in thread synchronization or wake-up conditions in ThreadOpenConnections could prevent the node from establishing outbound P2P connections after toggling network activity.
